newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane retraces earlier gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane retraces earlier gains.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices retraced intraday gains in thin late trade on Monday as NYMEX crude oil futures moved down on profit taking, players said.
"With crude falling off the way it did people got nervous and left the market," said one Houston trader.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane fell a half cent to between 52.25 cents and 52.50 cents a gallon. At midday, prices had risen a penny on concerns of cold weather.
Conway, Kansas, hub spot material fell about a quarter cent to 53.00/53.50 cents after rising 0.75 cent at midday.

The fall came despite the arrival of colder weather in the north. Up to two feet of snow fell on parts of Ohio, Michigan and New York over the weekend and more snowfall is expected through early Wednesday.
Demand for propane rises in the winter because the fuel is used to heat many rural homes.
NYMEX December crude oil futures ended down 22 cents at $23.37 a barrel on profit-taking.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
